content: An eyelash, also referred to as a lash, is one of the small hairs that grow along the edge of the eyelid. These hairs serve a protective function by shielding the eye from debris. Additionally, eyelashes are highly sensitive to touch, similar to the function of whiskers in animals like cats or mice. This sensitivity acts as a warning mechanism, prompting the eye to reflexively close when an object, such as an insect or dust particle, comes near. In humans, eyelashes begin to develop in the embryo between the 7th and 8th weeks of gestation. If an eyelash falls out or is pulled out, it will regrow, typically taking about four to eight weeks to do so. The color of eyelashes may differ from the color of scalp hair, though they are often darker in individuals with dark hair and lighter in those with light hair. The follicles of eyelashes are associated with specialized glands, including the glands of Zeiss and the glands of Moll. Long eyelashes are often considered a symbol of femininity across many cultures. As a result, some women seek to enhance their eyelash length artificially to appear more feminine and sexually attractive. This can be achieved through methods such as eyelash extensions. Historically, substances like kohl have been used since the Bronze Age to protect and enhance eyelashes. Modern eye makeup often includes mascara, eyeliner, and eyeshadow to emphasize the eyes. The 20th century saw the advent of realistic-looking false eyelashes, which became particularly popular in the 1960s. Several medical conditions and disorders can affect the eyelashes. Madarosis refers to the loss of eyelashes. Blepharitis is an inflammation of the eyelid margin, where the eyelashes meet the eyelid, often causing redness, itching, flaking skin, and potential eyelash loss. Distichiasis is the abnormal growth of eyelashes from areas of the eyelid where they do not typically grow. Trichiasis refers to ingrown eyelashes. Eyelashes can also become infested with crab lice. An external hordeolum, or stye, is a purulent inflammation caused by infection of the eyelash follicles and the associated sebaceous (Zeiss) and apocrine (Moll) glands. Trichotillomania is a psychological disorder characterized by an irresistible urge to pull out hair, including eyelashes. Demodex folliculorum, a microscopic mite that lives harmlessly in hair follicles, including those of the eyelashes, is present in about 98% of people. However, these mites can occasionally contribute to blepharitis. Eyelash and eyebrow transplant surgeries are available to reconstruct or thicken these hairs. In animals, eyelashes are a feature of mammals, as they are a type of hair. Camels have notably long and thick eyelashes, while giraffes are often admired for their beautiful lashes. Horses, cows, and even ostriches (which have vestigial feathers without barbs) also possess eyelashes. Certain dog breeds are prone to inherited eyelash problems. Eyelash vipers, a type of snake, have modified scales above their eyes that resemble eyelashes. Hornbills, a type of bird, have prominent feather-like eyelashes, which is an uncommon trait among birds. In mythology and cultural references, eyelashes have been attributed symbolic meanings. For example, the Greek goddess Hera was described as having cow's eyes (boôpis), and in Thai art, Buddha is depicted with eyelashes like a cow's. In Norse mythology, the giant Ymir's eyebrows were said to have formed Midgard, the world of men, and his eyelashes were set up by the gods to keep giants at the edges of the earth. Porcelain dolls often feature moving eyelids with detailed eyelashes, and cartoon characters like Betty Boop are depicted with exaggerated eyelashes and fluttering eyelids. Snoopy's sister, Belle, is distinguished by her long eyelashes. Some believe that finding a fallen eyelash is a sign of good luck. It is also said that if you find a fallen eyelash in your hand, you can make a wish by softly stating it and blowing the eyelash away. However, this does not work if the eyelash is intentionally pulled out.
